newsitem.title: USA: U.S. House tax chief proposes sweeping tax cuts.
newsitem.headline: U.S. House tax chief proposes sweeping tax cuts.

text.p: The influential chairman of the House Ways and Means Committee, Bill Archer, announced on Monday his plan for a net $85 billion in U.S. tax cuts including a reduction in the maximum capital gains tax rate as well as education and child tax relief.
"Tax relief and a balanced budget are on the way for the American people," Archer declared at a press conference to unveil the tax cut package.

Archer's package was expected to be the starting point for drafting of tax cuts agreed between President Bill Clinton and the Republican Congress as part of the plan to balance the budget in five years. Archer said he was confident his plan would be signed into law. But Democrats are expected to resist some of the proposals.

A centerpiece of the package is a cut in the capital gains tax on assets such as stocks. He proposed the maximum capital gains rate of 28 percent for individuals be reduced to 20 percent. For corporations, Archer proposed the rate be cut from 35 percent to 30 percent for assets held more than five years.

"With the recent stock market boom, an increasing number of middle-class Americans are benefiting from the rising value of their stocks and mutual funds," Archer said. "Middle-income Americans need a capital gains tax cut, and I intend to give it to them."
Other features of the tax package include a child tax credit and tax credits for the costs of college education. It would also phase out the alternative minimum tax for corporations.
